name: shell-operator-742b3baf-blind29-ots
instr:
# Diagnosing shell-operator's injected misbehaviour without a test suite

I keep an installation that launches small scripts in response to what happens in a cluster, and it now gets a great many things wrong at once. Nothing about the cluster changed and nothing about my scripts changed. The repository has received 29 separate undocumented edits. What follows is everything I could pin down from the outside, in the order I came across it.

Getting it going at all is the first trouble. Pointing it at a folder of scripts that plainly exists on disk comes back as a failure, as though no path had been handed over, so nothing is loaded and no initial work is ever lined up. When that folder holds an executable buried in a nested folder of shared material that the scan is meant to step over, the warning I used to get about that executable never appears. The listener that accepts callbacks from the cluster over TLS will not come up either: with a certificate and key pair in place and readable, bringing it up hands back an error instead of succeeding quietly. Two of the things I type on the command line are thrown away as well — the client certificate authority path for the endpoint that reviews changes before the cluster accepts them ends up holding whatever the surroundings had rather than what I typed, and the client certificate authority path for the endpoint that translates a resource between stored revisions is dropped the same way.

Declaring what a script wants now fails on do
